summary: Owner NAS Ubuntu VM (Haswell-class Xeon, AVX2 without VNNI), candidates A, B, C and D measured on the same 60 core cases as the cloud receipts (threads 1, 2, 4, 8; swap-free, quiet-machine runs only). A and B reproduce the cloud picks exactly (A 28/60 de, 39/60 en; B 31/60, 39/60). The ORT dynamic-int8 files C and D produce near-uniform probabilities on this CPU (accuracy 25-33 %, Brier about 0.688, 38 % / 31 % agreement with B / A): the int8 recipe is numerically unusable here and int8 gives no latency advantage over fp32 B on this CPU either. A follow-up int8 variant with reduce_range=True (Cr) works (50.0 / 58.3 %, 77 % agreement with B) but is not faster than B. A, B, C and Cr fail the preliminary German gate; D formally passes it (gap 1.7 points, equal Brier) only because it is at chance level in both languages, which is not a pass.
honesty: Labels in decision-eval-cases.json are agent-authored proposals, not independently validated; accuracy is only a relative signal between candidates (60 core cases per language: one case = 1.67 percentage points).

The machine is the owner NAS VM (a KVM guest, not the physical NAS and not reference hardware). The guest changed in the middle of the session: runs marked cfg1 had 16 vCPUs and 3387 MiB RAM (swap 3.9 GiB active), after a VM restart by the owner (about 18:37-18:41 CEST, journal of the previous boot ends without a shutdown record) runs marked cfg2 had 64 vCPUs and 7393 MiB RAM. The CPU model and flags are the same; repeat runs of B, C and D at 2 threads on cfg2 agree with cfg1 within run-to-run spread.

B, C and D were built by us on the Mac (arm64) with the scripts in scripts/spikes/candidates-prep; the data file of B is byte-identical to the one built in the cloud sandbox, the graph files differ (torch dynamo export on macOS vs Linux, and the export script now drops stale shape annotations); picks of B are identical to the cloud and the Mac run (180 of 180).

File cache was not controlled for the first runs (C-t1..t8, D-t2..t8); from B-t1 attempt 4 on, the cached pages of the other candidates model files were evicted with posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) before each run to reduce page-cache pressure on the 3.4 GiB guest. Each run is a fresh process; first inference is reported separately; warm statistics are over the remaining 179 calls.

Temperatures are the shipped ones (multilingual: all 1.0, uncalibrated). Nothing was refitted. Long-input latency was not measured. The German gate (accuracy gap <= 5 points, Brier gap <= 0.05) is the preliminary gate from the handoff, not a product decision.

method.runner: scripts/spikes/decision-laya-candidates.mjs at the head of the PR branch (c4bba785 plus the candidates-prep export fixes), unchanged measurement code; no A-orig (hash-pinned runner) rows were run on the NAS this time
sameAsCloudReceipts: one request per call, 180 calls = 60 core + 30 extra pairs x 2 locales, in fixture order
first call reported separately; warm p50/p95 over calls 2..180 with nearest-rank percentiles (percentile() from decision-laya-lib.mjs)
intraOpNumThreads = threads, interOpNumThreads = 1, CPU execution provider, onnxruntime-node 1.30.0, Node 24.21.0
method.quietRule: Before each attempt: 1-minute load average < 0.5 and none of cargo/rustc/rustup/clippy-driver/pnpm/vitest/apt/apt-get/dpkg/packagekitd/gnome-software running (polled every 10 s); the desktop session stayed running. An attempt is discarded when the foreign CPU share in the inference loop >= 5 %, any 30-call chunk >= 10 % or steal >= 5 % (never triggered).
method.swapRule: vmstat 1 runs during every attempt; the first (since boot) sample is skipped; ANY nonzero si or so in the remaining samples discards the attempt, even if it happened during model load. 16 attempts were discarded for this reason (list below), all valid runs have si = so = 0.
method.loadNote: loadAvgAtStart is read inside the runner after its own start-up and can be slightly above 0.5; loadAvg1minBeforeLaunch is the value the quiet rule checked.

lostRuns.reason: attempt in progress when the orchestrator was stopped by us to add the page-cache eviction step; no result

environment.vm: Intel Xeon E5-2620 v3 @ 2.40GHz (Haswell-EP, family 6 model 63), KVM guest "Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996)", flags: sse4_2, avx, avx2, fma, f16c; no avx512*, no avx_vnni, no amx*

cfg1.memory: MemTotal 3387 MiB, swap 3.9 GiB (swappiness 60), 2.3-2.4 GiB MemAvailable at run start, swap in use 656-766 MiB before the runs started (no activity during valid runs), GNOME desktop session running

cfg2.memory: MemTotal 7393 MiB, swap 3.9 GiB unused, about 6.1-6.3 GiB MemAvailable at run start, desktop session running

environment.runtime: Node v24.21.0 linux-x64 official tarball (SHA-256 checked against SHASUMS256.txt), onnxruntime-node 1.30.0, @huggingface/transformers 4.3.1, npm install --ignore-scripts in a scratch directory, no lockfile
environment.builder: Mac arm64, CPython 3.12, torch 2.14.1, transformers 5.20.2, onnx 1.23.2, onnxruntime 1.31.0 (quantizer), onnxscript 0.7.2, laya 0.4.12
environment.files: models copied with scp; the runner hashes every file (artifacts in each run of the original receipts; here in the candidates block)
environment.cleanup: ~/plur1bus-laya-bench on the VM (models, node, runtime, outputs, logs) deleted after the measurement

A.note: Not measurable on the first guest configuration (3387 MiB: about 1.75 GiB RSS next to the desktop session swapped, see earlierAttempt). Measured after the owner enlarged the guest (MemAvailable >= 6 GiB >= the 3000 MiB precondition).

C.finding: Probabilities are near-uniform on this CPU (max confidence 0.002); picks agree with B in 37.8 % of 180 rows. On arm64 (Mac) the same file agrees with B in 95.6 %, on the AVX-512 VNNI cloud VM in 76.1 %.

D.derivedFrom: A (fp32 upcast) via upcast_fp16_to_fp32.py then quantize_dynamic_int8.py
D.finding: Same failure as C: near-uniform probabilities, 30.6 % agreement with A (Mac arm64: 93.9 %, cloud: 65.6 %).

Cr.how: quantize_dynamic_int8.py with reduce_range=True (the only change; not committed as a script change)
Cr.note: Extra variant to test whether the failure is the 8-bit weight range on AVX2 without VNNI. It is not one of the requested candidates. Mac arm64 run: 50.0 / 61.7 %.

earlierAttempt.note: First NAS attempt (guest cfg1, original runner): swapped, not a latency result. Kept for the record.
earlierAttempt.reason: vmstat shows swap activity in 156 of 272 sampled seconds (swap-in 585660 KiB, swap-out 943083 KiB in total); model load took 79.0 s; MemAvailable dropped to 782 MiB; swap in use grew from 298 MiB to 645 MiB, pushing the desktop session's memory out. The run is not a valid latency measurement.

ramRule: Run only with load1 < 0.5 before launch and no heavy foreign process; any vmstat si/so > 0 discards the run; A only with MemAvailable >= 3000 MiB.
next: Decide on the multilingual candidate with the German gate evidence in mind; on CPUs without VNNI do not ship the ORT dynamic-int8 recipe (C/D) as built; a statically quantized (QDQ) or reduce_range variant would have to be re-validated per target CPU. Independent labels, reference hardware and long-input latency are still open.
